text:
maya: Heads up — after merging Pelorus LoRA v2 into the customer channel, quick-eval pack shows a token-gap around invoice amounts. EMR on invoices down ~6%. sample output attached below. :frowning:

maya: sample prompt: "Summarize invoice 2023-09-14 total amount"
response (old): "Total: $12,345.67"
response (merged): "Total: $12,345 . 67"  <-- space inserted in number and sometimes dropped digits

maya: quick eval snippet (script):
```
$ python scripts/eval_quickpack.py --customer pelorus --model merged/pelorus-lora-v2 --seed 42 --metric invoice_exact_match
EMR: 0.842 (baseline 0.898)
Top-1 token-shift around token ids [208, 209, 210]
```

ravi: ugh. do we have the exact tokenizer used for the LoRA training? could be tokenizer mismatch when merging. @elena any idea? :eyes:

elena: likely. Pelorus training used tok v3 (customized whitespace merges). Merge might have been applied against mainline tok v2. quick check: run `python -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer; print(AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('pelorus/tok-v3').encode('12,345.67'))"`

elena: if the ids differ, that's our culprit — numbers tokenized into different pieces -> model sees different prefix KV patterns

maya: confirmed: pelorus/tok-v3 encodes `12,345.67` as [1012, 58, 345, 332, 77] vs main tok-v2 as [1012, 58345, 33277] -> split vs fused. merging against wrong tokenizer will shift KV cache alignment.

tj: can we retokenize evaluation set to pelorus/tok-v3 and re-run? cheap check before rolling back.

maya: running now.

opsbot: CI run started: job/eng-ml/eval-pelorus/3798765432 (ETA ~4m)

maya: result: re-eval with tok-v3 -> EMR back up to 0.897 (within noise of baseline). so evaluation tokenization explains the drop.

ravi: OK great. root cause = tokenizer mismatch at merge time, not model weight corruption. what's the merge flow that caused this? did the engineering merge use the wrong tokenizer file? @maya

maya: yes — merge script defaulted to `main/tokenizer.json` because the LoRA metadata didn't include explicit tokenizer ref. fix options: 1) re-run merge with tokenizers aligned; 2) update LoRA metadata to pin tokenizer ref and re-run CI; 3) pin deployment to previous model until we have metadata check in the pipeline.

tj: I'd vote for (2) + (3). add a pre-merge validation step that verifies tokenizer compatibility via token-overlap test.

elena: I can add tokenizer-compat check to the onboarding checklist. simple heuristic: sample 1k numeric tokens, compare split ratio > 0.05 -> flag.

maya: will open PR to add metadata validation and fail merges when tokenizer mismatch detected. also will add a one-off script to re-merge Pelorus properly and push a canary.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: merged/pelorus-lora-v2 -> canary-1 (hold for manual approve)

ravi: sounds good. timeline? we need customer to validate before EOD.

maya: aiming for canary in 2h. i'll post results here and ping @ravi. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

elena: also add a note to quick-eval README about always using training tokenizer for customer packs.

tj: nice catch. :party_parrot:
__notes: Thread: Pelorus customer LoRA merge tokenizer mismatch investigation and quick-eval re-run. Single-thread Slack style messages, short, with inline code and bot notices.
